clue.text: The young woman left with 9

parts.note: the answer to 9 across is a dolt, and a dolt is an ass

explanation.surface: A girl walks off arm in arm with the fool from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' sends you to 9 across, whose answer is a fool; take a short synonym for that, ASS, and put L for 'left' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lass is a girl, a young female, especially in Scottish and northern English usage.

clue.text: Handy source of dates?

parts.note: read 'Handy' as 'belonging to the hand' and think of the tree that bears dates; one word covers both the inside of the hand and that tree

explanation.surface: Asking where one might conveniently look up a diary appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a calendar or diary; the question mark flags the pun on 'Handy' (part of the hand) and dates the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm is the tree bearing dates, and the palm is the inner surface of the hand.

clue.text: Old port-a bargain

definitions.meaning: A town on the Kent coast, historically one of the Cinque Ports
an agreement or transaction, as in striking a good one

explanation.surface: An ancient harbour town picked up cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a seaside town in Kent, England, once an important naval anchorage; 'a' is just a link before the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic Kentish harbour town shares its name with the word for an agreed transaction.

clue.text: Say yet again others were given food

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
ate is the past tense of eat, taking food

explanation.surface: Repeating that the other people have now been fed.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something once more is to repeat it, saying it yet again.

clue.text: Plainly he has no secret accounts!

definitions.text: Plainly he has no secret accounts!

parts.words: Plainly he has no secret accounts!
parts.note: the surface suggests an honest man with nothing hidden; read 'accounts' as customers' money and 'secret' as the clerk telling all, a person who deals openly with deposits

explanation.surface: Praising an obviously honest person who hides nothing financially.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is double: the cashier handles bank accounts in public, and a 'teller' also tells, so he keeps no secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier at a bank counter, who pays out and receives money for customers.

clue.text: Being game, ten perhaps will be in the running

parts.note: a being, a human, is a man

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of game and ten could be in some other order

explanation.surface: A willing sportsman, maybe one of ten, hopes to be in contention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' and 'running' both pull towards sport; 'the running' of a business is its control, and 'perhaps' is the signal to reorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Management is the control and direction of an enterprise, its day-to-day operation.

clue.text: An orange tin with a green mould

indicators.note: to mould is to reshape, so the letters of tin, a and green are reshaped

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit in a can that has gone green and mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mould' looks like fungus on old fruit but is a verb asking you to reshape TIN + A + GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, loose-skinned variety of citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: A direction to be off!

parts.note: a way is a route or direction, as in 'this way'

explanation.surface: An order telling someone to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a command: 'Away!' tells someone to be off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gone or absent from a place is to be elsewhere, as in 'he is off on holiday'.

clue.text: The person wanting endless fruit one cannot supply

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for fruit is dropped

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
what one says when unable to supply something: 'I can't'

explanation.surface: A customer asks for fruit that a shop cannot provide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims APPLE to APPL; then 'one cannot supply' is the excuse I CAN'T, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is someone who applies for, and so seeks, a job, place or grant.

clue.text: One's retiring representative revealed as a dolt

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the short form for 'one is' is turned round

parts.note: one is becomes I and IS, read as I'S
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A shy politician is exposed as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like a shy MP but reverses I'S into SI; MP is a Member of Parliament, the UK's elected representative; LET ON means revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, slow-witted person, a dunce.

clue.text: Crack up it's on the level

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a crack is a sharp blow or knock, a rap

explanation.surface: A joke falls flat but is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAP in this down entry. PAR is the standard or equal level, as in 'on a par'.
explanation.definitionFit: Par means equality or an even standard, as with shares trading at face value.

clue.text: A Greek character kept half the fish

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters of kept are used

explanation.surface: A Greek man held on to half of the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece but means the Greek letter PI; 'half' keeps KE of KEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pike is a large predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: Set a member back

indicators.note: back means the word for a limb is read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Putting a limb back into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses LEG; 'Set' means to become firm, as jelly does.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set or solidify, as a jelly does when it cools.

clue.text: She's a great deal in the car unfortunately

indicators.note: in means the word for a great deal is placed inside the rearranged letters
unfortunately implies things have gone wrong, so the letters of the and car are jumbled

parts.note: a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: A woman gets a fantastic bargain on a car, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a great deal' reads as a bargain on the car, but it is just a synonym for much; 'She' signals a woman's given name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a female given name, so it stands for a particular woman.

clue.text: Bloomers made by people in road-transport

indicators.note: in means the word for peoples is placed within the word for vehicles

parts.note: cars are a form of road transport
nations are peoples, as in the peoples of the world

explanation.surface: Gaffes committed by drivers on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' suggests blunders or old-fashioned knickers; here it means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnations are popular cut flowers, things that bloom.

clue.text: Change in pay that causes disgust

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters of in pay that

explanation.surface: A pay cut provokes revulsion among the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' suggests altered wages but asks you to rearrange IN PAY THAT; 'causes' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is strong dislike or aversion, close to revulsion.

clue.text: Slip resulting from a lack of good grounding

definitions.text: Slip resulting from a lack of good grounding

parts.words: Slip resulting from a lack of good grounding
parts.note: read as an error caused by poor education, it is really earth sliding when the ground underneath is unstable

explanation.surface: A mistake made because someone was poorly taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounding' looks like basic training; literally it is unstable earth giving way down a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall of earth and rock down a hillside, a slip of the land.

clue.text: Fancy a little holiday at the seaside again

indicators.note: a little means only a small part of the phrase holiday at the seaside again is used, its letters running across the final two words

explanation.surface: Would you like another short break by the sea?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb inviting you on holiday; it is the noun, a notion. The letters sit across 'seaside again'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, a thought in the mind.

clue.text: Duck classification, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like the letter O
a rating is a grading or classification

explanation.surface: Sorting birds of the duck family, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a bird but is cricket's score of nought, giving O. The definition is literal: making a formal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Orating means making a speech, delivering words formally or pompously.

clue.text: Wonder vehicle seen turning in the distance

indicators.note: in means the reversed vehicle is placed inside the word for distance

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance

indicators.note: turning means the word for a vehicle is turned round

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An amazing car appears turning far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the distance' reads as far away, but 'in' is the container signal and 'the distance' a unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a marvel, an extraordinary event that amazes.

clue.text: The shoot occupied by an object in the sky-a bird

indicators.note: occupied by means the word for a shoot is filled with the celestial body

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
a star is an object seen in the night sky

explanation.surface: Gunfire is aimed at a flying object, which turns out to be a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' suggests firing at birds, but it is the plant sense, a young growth.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large, heavy ground bird of open country.

clue.text: The light here could be "Strike softly"

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Instructions for a light are written as 'hit gently'.
explanation.walkthrough: LAM is slang for thrash; P is piano, the musical direction for soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device giving light, such as a table lamp.

clue.text: Getting awfully wet, so sure to acquire rainproof wear

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of wet, so and sure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone soaked to the skin decides to buy a waterproof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles WET + SO + SURE; 'Getting' and 'to acquire' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is a waterproof hat with a broad brim at the back, worn by sailors in storms.

clue.text: Hence the head of state will make an appeal for help

parts.note: hence means therefore, so

indicators.note: the head of means just the first letter of state is used

explanation.surface: Therefore the country's leader will issue a call for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a president but simply gives S, the first letter of 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: SOS is the international Morse distress signal, a call for rescue.

clue.text: A couple of pounds, no more

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra), so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: Only two pounds, nothing extra.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for a pound sterling, from the Latin libra; 'no more' is ALL as in 'that's all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'that is all' means there is nothing further, the entirety.

clue.text: Choose a table

definitions.meaning: an archaic verb meaning to wish or please, as in 'the wind blows where it will'
a tabulated set of items, an itemised record

explanation.surface: Selecting a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is old-fashioned: to choose or desire, as in the biblical 'the wind bloweth where it listeth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb meant to wish or choose, and a schedule or catalogue of items is the noun sense.

clue.text: Even in its crude form it's quite concentrated

indicators.note: a crude form is a rough, unrefined version, so the letters of even in its are rearranged

explanation.surface: Even unrefined, this substance is strong stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude form' suggests crude oil but asks you to rearrange EVEN IN ITS; 'it's quite' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive means concentrated or thorough, focused hard on one area.

clue.text: A note placed in back-issue indicates agreement

indicators.note: placed in means the musical note is put inside the reversed word
back means the word for offspring is written backwards

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A footnote in an old magazine shows the editor concurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-issue' looks like an old magazine; it is SON (issue, offspring) turned back to NOS, with D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a gesture of assent, signalling yes.

clue.text: Some get morbid-let themselves go-when unemployed

indicators.note: some means only part of the phrase morbid-let is used, straddling the hyphen

explanation.surface: Some people grow gloomy and neglect themselves when out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'morbID-LEt'; 'get', 'themselves go' and 'when' are surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working, without a job or not in use.

clue.text: Cheese made in a new way

indicators.note: in a new way means the letters of made are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A cheese produced by a novel method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' looks like part of the surface but is the fodder that 'in a new way' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, sold in red-waxed balls.

clue.text: Ill-will of loveless diplomat

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O, and less says it is removed

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent on a mission

explanation.surface: Bitterness felt by a diplomat with no romance in his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is zero in tennis, written O; 'loveless' takes O out of ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for another's advantages, a form of malice.

clue.text: Foreign stock exchange?

parts.note: read not as an overseas bourse but as American currency held and traded abroad, in a bank outside its home country

explanation.surface: Asking about an overseas share market.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'stock': not shares but money, specifically dollars held and exchanged in European banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A US dollar deposited in a bank outside America, traded on international money markets.
